title: Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) — Determination and Payment of Premiums
content:
# Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) — Determination and Payment of Premiums

## Clause 1 — The monthly premium

1.1 The monthly premium is the tier's amount for the insured's age band on each premium due date.

1.2 Each of the six tiers — VGLI $50,000 Coverage, VGLI $100,000 Coverage, VGLI $200,000 Coverage, VGLI $300,000 Coverage, VGLI $400,000 Coverage and VGLI $500,000 Coverage — is priced from its own face amount and its own amounts by age band in the product's premium rate schedule; a policy is never priced from another tier's amounts.

1.3 When the insured enters a new age band, the premium changes on the first due date after the birthday.

## Clause 2 — Other billing frequencies

2.1 A quarterly, semiannual or annual premium is the monthly premium times 3, 6 or 12 months, with no discount.

2.2 A partial month is billed as a full month.

| Billing frequency | Premium billed | Discount |
|---|---|---|
| monthly | the monthly premium | none |
| quarterly | the monthly premium multiplied by 3 | none |
| semiannual | the monthly premium multiplied by 6 | none |
| annual | the monthly premium multiplied by 12 | none |

## Clause 3 — Ways to pay

3.1 Premiums may be paid by electronic funds transfer, direct bill, deduction from VA compensation or pension, or allotment from military retired pay.

## Worked figures (hypothetical insured)

*Inputs are hypothetical: an insured holding VGLI $100,000 Coverage whose age on the due date places them in the 40 to 44 band, where the schedule's monthly amount for that tier is $17.00.*

| Billing frequency | Working | Premium |
|---|---|---|
| monthly | $17.00 | $17.00 |
| quarterly | $17.00 multiplied by 3 | $51.00 |
| semiannual | $17.00 multiplied by 6 | $102.00 |
| annual | $17.00 multiplied by 12 | $204.00 |

The annual premium of $204.00 is exactly twelve monthly premiums; paying annually earns no reduction.

*Band change (hypothetical):* the same insured turns 45 on the 15th of a month. The premium due on the 1st of that month is still priced in the 40 to 44 band. The first due date after the birthday is the 1st of the following month, and from that due date the premium is the tier's amount for the 45 to 49 band.

*Partial month (hypothetical):* where coverage runs for only part of a month, that month is billed as a full month at the monthly premium.

## Basis questions

- *Is there a saving for paying a year at a time?* No. The annual premium is the monthly premium times 12, with no discount.
- *Does the premium change on the insured's birthday itself?* The premium changes on the first due date after the birthday on which the insured enters a new age band.
- *Can the premium come out of a VA compensation or pension payment?* Yes. Deduction from VA compensation or pension is one of the four ways premiums may be paid.
